policies.sentence: Generative AI means any text, image or code generating system; course-built models and all coursework are covered or exempted as stated.
The instructor discloses when and where the instructor uses AI.
The instructor will never use AI to grade.
Teaching staff steer students back on track when they seem to give up on their learning.
Students should ask course staff or humans, in office hours or on the forum, before turning to AI.
The instructor provides guidance on AI through course materials and office hours and welcomes discussion or disagreement.
Staff and peer tutors are available to help students.
The instructor provides no explicit support or training in using AI tools.
The instructor may amend the AI policy during the semester; the current policy may be only interim.
The teaching staff's evaluation of assignments is the final grade determination.
Solutions that solve a different problem or do not follow the specification are not graded.
Students may always use the textbook and resources provided by the instructor.
Students must not search online for solutions.
Students must not use AI for note-taking.
Students must not use AI in in-class discussions unless explicitly allowed.
Students must prevent AI interactions that produce code responses.
Students are invited to share AI stories, helpful resources, feedback and observed AI bias.
Fair evaluation of student work needs work not assisted by AI; past bans disadvantaged honest students.
Powerful AI technology calls for caution and informed consent, and AI empowers bad actors.
The instructor wants students' own ideas, not what a chatbot says.
A generous late policy is designed in part to reduce the temptation to use AI.
Citing AI use will not prevent a low score.
Detailed AI policy is given elsewhere in the syllabus.
The class decides the policy on using AI coding assistants.
Students may post short code snippets of two lines or less when asking about syntax errors.
Each prompt earns at most ten minutes of the time Claude spends working on it.
Students may change flagged parts of their work and resubmit as necessary.
